payload.detail: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): No hydration changes since the audit. Lines moved: forceRefresh now rag.ts:1142 and rag-cache.ts:1057; per-request caches rag.ts:1116-1118. The row itself values the saving at a fraction of a second, so P3. PRIOR DETAIL: MEASURED BY CODE AUDIT 2026-09-17, not inferred, against HEAD 8427182d8. For POST /api/search mode=differentials, query 'major depressive disorder', anonymous caller, cold cache: floor approx 27 round trips, typical 34-37, worst approx 45. The four parallel retrieval strategies (lexical, embedding-field, index-unit, hybrid) are deliberate and should NOT be collapsed; the cost is in follow-up hydration. FOUR CONCRETE WASTES, each verified in source: (1) loadChunksForSignalMatches (rag-candidate-sources.ts:1345 -> :1362 -> :1393) is a 3-hop serial chain paid TWICE, where attachDocumentContextPackAdmission in the same file at :275-278 already does the identical job in one embedded-join query; 4 serial hops on the critical path where 2 would do. (2) attachPageVisualEvidence (rag-hydration.ts:253-306) has NO cache and runs 3x per search over heavily overlapping document/page sets. (3) cacheIndexingVersion(...,{forceRefresh:true}) runs twice per search (rag.ts:1088 and rag-cache.ts:1057) and deletes its own 5s TTL entry before reading, so the cache is write-only on the search path; the rag-cache.ts:1057 one is justified as a mid-request staleness guard, the rag.ts:1088 one is not. (4) loadChunksForMemoryCards ignores the request-scoped ChunkLoadCache entirely and runs twice (lexical then vector keys). Also: the typo-correction recursion at rag.ts:1245 threads cacheContext but re-creates memoryCardCache/chunkLoadCache/documentRankingMetadataCache at rag.ts:1062-1064, so an out_of_corpus query pays ~2x the whole search with every hydration cache cold. REFUTED HYPOTHESIS, recorded so it is not re-investigated: the versioned _v2/_v3 retrieval RPCs are NOT missing. All twelve preferred names were cross-checked against supabase/schema.sql and all 248 migration files and every one resolves with matching argument names; drift-allowlist.json has zero functions entries, so a missing one would fail check:drift. Also corrected: callVersionedRetrievalRpc costs 2x not 3x for an anonymous caller (it returns after the legacy call when owner_filter is the public sentinel, rag-candidate-sources.ts:587-594). PRIORITY RATIONALE: P2 not P1 because this is second-order. The dominant cost was read_site_content_public_records at up to 92s; this whole item is worth a fraction of a second and is only worth doing after the catalogue migration lands. NEXT: items 1 and 2 above are the highest value. ALL of these live in src/lib/rag/** which is a RAG-ranking protected surface: flag to owner BEFORE editing, RAG impact line required, owner-merge, and item 1 needs an eval canary because reproducing the three filters (documents.status=indexed, the owner-scope ladder, and the index_generation_id check at :1418) imperfectly would silently drop candidates and change ranking. STOP: do not remove the legacy rungs of callVersionedRetrievalRpc (zero cost while v2 exists, and they are the fail-soft path), and do not skip the coverage-gate block for broad_summary (its results re-enter the candidate pool at rag.ts:1555 and removing it changes ranking).
